📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost Ingress Chart — Function Typo BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost uses an Ingress to route traffic: api.anihpj.com goes to the Django API, anihpj.com goes to the Django Web frontend. The Ingress template converts the environment name to uppercase for use in TLS certificate names and annotations using the Sprig upper function. But a typo — uppper with three p's — breaks the entire chart. Even though the rest of the chart is perfectly valid, this one-character mistake prevents the Ingress from rendering, and without an Ingress, external traffic can't reach the application at all.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for Ingress chart (S5): 
s5-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml              ← Environment name: "production"
└── templates/
    └── ingress.yaml          ← Uses {{ .Values.env | uppper }} ← TYPO!
BASH — Create chart with Sprig function typo bug 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S5: Sprig Function Typo — "uppper" not defined
# STANDALONE LAB — creates isolated chart directory
# ============================================

mkdir -p ~/helm-lab/s5-chart/templates
cd ~/helm-lab

cat << 'EOF' > ./s5-chart/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: anihpj-ingress
description: Ingress for anihpj/jobpost — routes API and Web traffic
type: application
version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "2.5"
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s5-chart/values.yaml
env: "production"                        # Used with upper() for TLS cert naming
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: "nginx"
  hosts:
    - host: "api.anihpj.com"
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          serviceName: anihpj-api
          servicePort: 8000
    - host: "anihpj.com"
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          serviceName: anihpj-web
          servicePort: 80
  tls:
    - secretName: anihpj-tls
      hosts:
        - "api.anihpj.com"
        - "anihpj.com"
EOF

# ingress.yaml — BUG: "uppper" instead of "upper"
cat << 'EOF' > ./s5-chart/templates/ingress.yaml
{{- if .Values.ingress.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-ingress
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-{{ .Values.env | uppper }}"  # ❌ TYPO!
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
  labels:
    environment: {{ .Values.env | uppper | quote }}                # ❌ TYPO!
spec:
  ingressClassName: {{ .Values.ingress.className }}
  tls:
    {{- range .Values.ingress.tls }}
    - secretName: {{ .secretName }}-{{ $.Values.env | uppper }}   # ❌ TYPO!
      hosts:
        {{- range .hosts }}
        - {{ . | quote }}
        {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
  rules:
    {{- range .Values.ingress.hosts }}
    - host: {{ .host | quote }}
      http:
        paths:
          {{- range .paths }}
          - path: {{ .path }}
            pathType: {{ .pathType }}
            backend:
              service:
                name: {{ .serviceName }}
                port:
                  number: {{ .servicePort }}
          {{- end }}
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
EOF

# TRY TO RENDER:
echo "============================================"
echo "RENDERING — EXPECT 'function not defined'..."
echo "============================================"
helm template test ./s5-chart 2>&1
echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo "↑ Error: function 'uppper' not defined ↑"
echo "============================================"

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s5-chart → FAILS with "function not defined"
✗2. Error: "function 'uppper' not defined" at ingress.yaml line 7
✗3. All THREE uses of "uppper" fail — annotations, labels, and TLS secretName
✗4. Without the Ingress, external users can't reach anihpj.com → job board inaccessible!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Read the error: helm template test ./s5-chart 2>&1 | grep "not defined"
→ "function 'uppper' not defined" — the function name has 3 p's!
2Find all uses: grep -n 'uppper' ./s5-chart/templates/ingress.yaml
→ 3 occurrences: lines 7, 10, and 17 — all have the typo
3Check correct spelling: Sprig documentation lists the function as upper (single 'p')
→ Correct: "upper" — Wrong: "uppper" — one extra 'p'
4Root cause: Typo in Sprig function name — "uppper" instead of "upper". Sprig function names are EXACT string matches; even one wrong character causes "not defined"
5Fix: Replace all instances of "uppper" with "upper"
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm template fails → "function 'uppper' not defined"
②
Read the function name carefully — "uppper" has 3 p's!
③
Check Sprig docs → correct name is "upper" (2 p's)
④
grep for the typo → found 3 occurrences in ingress.yaml
⑤
Replace "uppper" → "upper" → Chart renders → Ingress deploys!

Tenet: Helm embeds the Sprig function library — 70+ template functions with exact, case-sensitive names. upper, lower, quote, nindent, default, required, toYaml, sha256sum, semverCompare — every character must match exactly. helm lint catches these typos BEFORE you attempt a dry-run. Always lint first: helm lint ./chart would have caught "uppper" instantly. The most common Sprig function typos: nindent→indent (wrong function), quote→qoute (transposed letters), upper→uppper (double letter), default→deafult (transposed vowels).

$ grep -n 'uppper' ./s5-chart/templates/ingress.yaml 7: cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-{{ .Values.env | uppper }}" 10: environment: {{ .Values.env | uppper | quote }} 17: - secretName: {{ .secretName }}-{{ $.Values.env | uppper }} ← 3 typos found!
$ helm lint ./s5-chart ==> Linting ./s5-chart [ERROR] templates/: function "uppper" not defined Error: 1 chart(s) linted, 1 chart(s) failed ← lint catches it!

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost Multi-Host Ingress — Nil Range BUG

The Ingress template iterates over .Values.ingress.hosts to generate rules dynamically. But the values.yaml file defines the hosts under .Values.hosts instead of .Values.ingress.hosts — the entire .Values.ingress key is nil! When {{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }} tries to iterate over nil, Go templates panic.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for Multi-Host Ingress chart (S6): 
s6-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml              ← hosts defined at wrong path!
└── templates/
    └── ingress.yaml          ← range .Values.ingress.hosts ← NIL!

# ============================================

cd ~/helm-lab

cat << 'EOF' > ./s6-chart/Chart.yaml

  className: "nginx"

        servicePort: 8000
  - host: "anihpj.com"

      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix

  - host: "admin.anihpj.com"

        pathType: Prefix

        servicePort: 8000
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s6-chart/templates/ingress.yaml

  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-ingress
spec:
  ingressClassName: {{ .Values.ingress.className }}

    {{- range .Values.ingress.hosts }}    # ❌ BUG! .Values.ingress.hosts is NIL!
    - host: {{ .host | quote }}
      http:
        paths:
          {{- range .paths }}
          - path: {{ .path }}
            pathType: {{ .pathType }}
            backend:
              service:

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s6-chart → PANICS with "range can't iterate over nil"
✗2. Error at line 10 — {{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }} targets nil value
✗3. Check values.yaml — hosts exist but NOT under ingress key!
✗4. Without the Ingress, external traffic can't reach any anihpj service!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Read the error: helm template test ./s6-chart 2>&1 | grep "nil"
→ "range can't iterate over nil" at .Values.ingress.hosts
2Check what .Values.ingress contains: yq eval '.ingress' ./s6-chart/values.yaml
→ enabled: true, className: "nginx" — NO hosts key under ingress!
3Check where hosts ARE defined: yq eval '.hosts' ./s6-chart/values.yaml
→ 3 hosts found at ROOT level — NOT under .Values.ingress!
4Root cause: hosts array is defined at .Values.hosts (root level) but template references .Values.ingress.hosts (nested under ingress) — the ingress key has no hosts field, so .Values.ingress.hosts is nil, and range panics on nil
5Fix: Move the hosts array under ingress: key in values.yaml OR change template to {{ range .Values.hosts }}
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm template panics → "range can't iterate over nil"
②
{{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }} → Check .Values.ingress in values.yaml
③
.Values.ingress has enabled + className but NO hosts → hosts is nil!
④
Search for hosts elsewhere → Found at .Values.hosts (root level)
⑤
Move hosts under ingress: or add nil guard → Ingress renders 3 hosts!

Tenet: {{ range }} requires a non-nil slice, array, map, or channel. If the value is nil (missing key, undefined), Go templates panic with "range can't iterate over nil." ALWAYS guard range with an if check: {{ if .Values.ingress.hosts }}{{ range .Values.ingress.hosts }}...{{ end }}{{ end }}. Even better: ensure the parent key exists before iterating over children. The most common cause: values defined at the WRONG nesting level in values.yaml — a single indentation mistake cascades to nil pointer failures.

$ yq eval '.ingress' ./s6-chart/values.yaml enabled: true className: nginx # ← NO hosts key here!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s6-chart | grep "host:" - host: "api.anihpj.com" - host: "anihpj.com" - host: "admin.anihpj.com" ✅ All 3 hosts rendered!
🔧

  className: "nginx"
  hosts:                                    # ✅ NOW under ingress!
    - host: "api.anihpj.com"
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          serviceName: anihpj-api
          servicePort: 8000
    - host: "anihpj.com"
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          serviceName: anihpj-web
          servicePort: 80
    - host: "admin.anihpj.com"
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          serviceName: anihpj-admin
          servicePort: 8000
EOF

# VERIFY THE FIX:
helm template test ./s6-chart | grep "host:"

# ALTERNATIVE: Add nil guard in template:

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost with Named Template — Case Mismatch BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost uses named templates in _helpers.tpl to generate consistent resource names. The template anihpj.fullname combines release name and chart name into a unique identifier. But a subtle typo — "fullname" vs "fullName" — breaks the entire chart. The deployment calls anihpj.fullname (lowercase 'n') but _helpers.tpl defines anihpj.fullName (uppercase 'N'). In Go templates, "fullname" and "fullName" are completely different identifiers — and Helm can't find the template.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for Named Template chart (S7): 
s7-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl          ← define "anihpj.fullName" ← UPPERCASE N!
    └── deployment.yaml       ← include "anihpj.fullname" ← lowercase n!
BASH — Create chart with template name case mismatch 
mkdir -p ~/helm-lab/s7-chart/templates
cd ~/helm-lab

cat << 'EOF' > ./s7-chart/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: anihpj-api
description: Django API Deployment for anihpj/jobpost
type: application
version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "2.5"
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s7-chart/values.yaml
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: anihpj-api
  tag: "2.5"
servicePort: 8000
EOF

# _helpers.tpl — defines "anihpj.fullName" (capital N!)
cat << 'EOF' > ./s7-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "anihpj.fullName" -}}        # ❌ fullName — capital N!
{{- printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name .Chart.Name | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" -}}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "anihpj.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end -}}
EOF

# deployment.yaml — calls "anihpj.fullname" (lowercase n!)
cat << 'EOF' > ./s7-chart/templates/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }}    # ❌ fullname — lowercase n!
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
          ports:
            - containerPort: {{ .Values.servicePort }}
EOF

echo "============================================"
echo "RENDERING — EXPECT 'template not defined'..."
echo "============================================"
helm template test ./s7-chart 2>&1
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s7-chart → FAILS with "template not defined"
✗2. Error: "template 'anihpj.fullname' not defined" — but you can SEE it in _helpers.tpl!
✗3. The Deployment can't get its name — Helm aborts before any YAML is generated
✗4. Without a name, the entire deployment is blocked!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Read the error: helm template test ./s7-chart 2>&1 | grep "not defined"
→ "template 'anihpj.fullname' not defined"
2Check what's defined in _helpers.tpl: grep 'define' ./s7-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
→ {{ define "anihpj.fullName" }} — has capital N!
3Check what's called in deployment.yaml: grep 'include.*full' ./s7-chart/templates/deployment.yaml
→ {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }} — has lowercase n!
4Root cause: Template names are CASE-SENSITIVE exact strings. "fullName" ≠ "fullname" — one capital letter difference breaks the entire match
5Fix: Make both names match EXACTLY — change define to "anihpj.fullname" or change include to "anihpj.fullName"
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm template fails → "template not defined"
②
Check _helpers.tpl → template IS defined, but name differs!
③
Compare define name vs include name character by character
④
"fullName" vs "fullname" → ONE character mismatch (N vs n)
⑤
Make names match exactly → Template renders → Deployment named!

Tenet: Named template identifiers are case-sensitive exact-match strings in Go templates. {{ define "anihpj.fullName" }} and {{ include "anihpj.fullname" . }} are completely different identifiers — Go treats them as unrelated. This is the #1 "it's right there, why doesn't it work?!" bug in Helm templates. Always copy-paste template names to avoid typos. Use helm lint — it catches "template not defined" before you even attempt a dry-run.

1

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost Service Chart — indent BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost uses a Service to expose the Django API. The Service template includes labels from a named template using include ... | indent 4. But indent only adds spaces — it does NOT add a newline before the indented content. The rendered output glues "app.kubernetes.io/name: anihpj-api" directly onto the same line as "labels:", producing YAML that kubectl rejects with "error converting YAML to JSON."
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for Service chart (S8): 
s8-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl          ← Named template "anihpj.labels"

name: anihpj-service

version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "2.5"
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s8-chart/values.yaml

  type: ClusterIP
  port: 8000
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s8-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "anihpj.labels" }}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: {{ .Release.Service }}
{{- end }}
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s8-chart/templates/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
  labels:{{ include "anihpj.labels" . | indent 4 }}  # ❌ BUG! indent, not nindent!
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.service.type }}
  ports:
    - port: {{ .Values.service.port }}
      targetPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
  selector:
    {{- include "anihpj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}

echo "============================================"
echo "RENDERING WITH indent BUG..."
echo "============================================"
helm template test ./s8-chart
echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo "↑ Look at 'labels:' line — labels are GLUED to it! ↑"
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s8-chart → YAML renders but is MALFORMED
✗2. Labels appear on the SAME line as labels: — glued together!
✗3. kubectl apply would reject this with "error converting YAML to JSON"
✗4. Compare with selector: which uses nindent — that one works perfectly!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check the labels line: helm template test ./s8-chart | grep -A3 "labels:"
→ labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: anihpj-service — ALL ON ONE LINE!
2Check the selector line: helm template test ./s8-chart | grep -A4 "selector:"
→ selector: (newline) then properly indented labels — works correctly!
3Compare the template calls: labels uses indent 4, selector uses nindent 4
→ indent adds spaces ONLY. nindent adds newline THEN spaces!
4Root cause: indent only adds leading spaces — it does NOT add a newline. The rendered content gets appended to the current line instead of starting on a new indented line. nindent (newline + indent) is needed for block-level template output
5Fix: Replace indent 4 with nindent 4 on the labels line
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
YAML renders but labels are glued → indent vs nindent
②
Labels line uses indent 4 → only adds spaces, no newline
③
Selector line uses nindent 4 → adds newline + spaces ✅
④
Rule: indent for inline values; nindent for block-level output
⑤
Change indent → nindent → Labels on separate lines → Valid YAML!

Tenet: indent N adds N spaces before each line. nindent N adds a NEWLINE then N spaces before each line. Use indent when the content should stay on the current line (inline values like {{ .Values.name | indent 2 }}). Use nindent when content must start on a NEW line (block-level includes like {{ include "labels" . | nindent 4 }}). The 'n' in nindent stands for "newline" — if you need a line break before your content, use nindent.

🔧

# VERIFY THE FIX:

# indent  = spaces only (for inline)
# nindent = newline + spaces (for block-level)

⑤
toYaml | nindent N → Properly indented resources → Valid YAML!

Tenet: toYaml ALWAYS needs nindent after it — never use toYaml alone in a template. The toYaml function converts a nested data structure (like resources or tolerations) into YAML starting at column 0. Without nindent, the output breaks the YAML document hierarchy. Count the spaces: determine what indentation level the block should be at, and use | nindent N. For containers[0].resources, that's typically 10 or 12 spaces depending on your template structure.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm template test ./s9-chart | grep -A6 "resources:" resources: limits: ← AT COLUMN 0 — WRONG! cpu: 1000m memory: 1Gi requests: ← AT COLUMN 0 — WRONG! cpu: 500m memory: 512Mi
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s9-chart | grep -A6 "resources:" resources: limits: ← Properly indented 12 spaces ✅ cpu: 1000m memory: 1Gi requests: cpu: 500m memory: 512Mi
🔧
BASH — Add | nindent 12 after toYaml 
# ONE-LINER FIX: add nindent pipe to toYaml
sed -i 's/{{ toYaml .Values.resources }}/{{ toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 12 }}/' ./s9-chart/templates/deployment.yaml

# VERIFY THE FIX:
helm template test ./s9-chart | grep -A6 "resources:"

# GOLDEN RULE: toYaml ALWAYS needs nindent after it.
# {{ toYaml .Values.x | nindent N }} ← CORRECT
# {{ toYaml .Values.x }}            ← WRONG (no indentation)

🧪 SCENARIO S10 — Category 1: Template Rendering Type Debug

YAML Type Coercion — Quote Missing on Integer Port

The Problem: You run helm template test ./s10-chart and the Service port is rendered as a bare integer 8000 instead of a quoted string "8000". While this works in most cases, certain Kubernetes fields (like ConfigMap data values, annotation values, and label values) MUST be strings. An unquoted integer in a string field causes kubectl apply to fail with "Invalid value: v1.ConfigMap.Data: values must be strings." Your job: find the unquoted value and wrap it with quote.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — YAML type debugging
1

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost ConfigMap — Missing quote BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost stores Django settings in a ConfigMap. The ConfigMap data values include database port, Redis port, and allowed hosts count — all numeric values from values.yaml. But the template renders these as bare integers: DATABASE_PORT: 5432 instead of DATABASE_PORT: "5432". While YAML can parse bare integers, Kubernetes ConfigMaps require ALL data values to be strings. kubectl rejects the ConfigMap with a type validation error, and Django can't read any configuration.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for ConfigMap chart (S10): 
s10-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml              ← Numeric port values
└── templates/
    └── configmap.yaml        ← Missing | quote on numeric values ← BUG!

  DATABASE_PORT: {{ .Values.database.port }}           # ❌ BUG! Integer — needs quote!
  DATABASE_NAME: {{ .Values.database.name }}           # String — OK
  REDIS_HOST: {{ .Values.redis.host }}                 # String — OK
  REDIS_PORT: {{ .Values.redis.port }}                 # ❌ BUG! Integer — needs quote!

EOF

echo "============================================"
echo "RENDERING — check data values for bare integers..."
echo "============================================"

echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo "↑ DATABASE_PORT: 5432 (bare integer — should be \"5432\") ↑"
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s10-chart → YAML renders but data values are bare integers!
✗2. DATABASE_PORT shows 5432 (integer) NOT "5432" (string)
✗3. kubectl apply rejects: "Invalid value: v1.ConfigMap.Data: values must be strings"
✗4. Django can't read the ConfigMap — app fails to start!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check data values: helm template test ./s10-chart | grep "PORT\|CONNECTIONS"
→ DATABASE_PORT: 5432, REDIS_PORT: 6379, MAX_CONNECTIONS: 100 — all bare integers!
2Check values.yaml types: yq eval '.database.port | tag' ./s10-chart/values.yaml
→ !!int — YAML interprets 5432 as an integer, not a string!
3Compare with working values: .database.host renders as "anihpj-db" (string) because it's already a string
→ String values pass through fine; numeric values need explicit quoting
4Root cause: values.yaml numeric fields are parsed as integers by YAML, and ConfigMap data values MUST be strings — Helm doesn't auto-quote them. Use | quote to force string conversion
5Fix: Add | quote to every numeric data value in the ConfigMap template
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
ConfigMap has bare integers → kubectl rejects it
②
YAML parses 5432 as integer, not string
③
ConfigMap data values MUST be strings per K8s API spec
④
Helm outputs the YAML type as-is — no auto-conversion
⑤
Add | quote → values become strings → ConfigMap accepted!

Tenet: The quote function is your YAML safety net. It wraps any value in double quotes, forcing YAML to treat it as a string. Always use | quote on values that could be misinterpreted: integers (port numbers), booleans (true/false could be YAML booleans), version numbers ("1.0" could be parsed as float 1.0), and any value going into a ConfigMap data field. The Sprig quote function adds surrounding double quotes; squote adds single quotes. For label values and annotation values, quote is equally important — a label value of "true" (string) vs true (boolean) can break label selectors.

📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s10-chart | grep "PORT\|CONNECTIONS" DATABASE_PORT: "5432" ← quoted string ✅ REDIS_PORT: "6379" ← quoted string ✅ MAX_CONNECTIONS: "100" ← quoted string ✅
🔧

sed -i 's/{{ .Values.redis.port }}/{{ .Values.redis.port | quote }}/' ./s10-chart/templates/configmap.yaml
sed -i 's/{{ .Values.maxConnections }}/{{ .Values.maxConnections | quote }}/' ./s10-chart/templates/configmap.yaml

# VERIFY THE FIX:
helm template test ./s10-chart | grep "PORT\|CONNECTIONS"

# GOLDEN RULE: Always quote values that could be non-strings.
# {{ .Values.port | quote }}  ← CORRECT
# {{ .Values.port }}          ← RISKY (may render as integer)

helm install Fails — Missing PostgreSQL Subchart Dependency

The Problem: You run helm install anihpj ./s11-chart and Helm fails because the anihpj/jobpost chart declares a dependency on a PostgreSQL subchart, but the dependency was never downloaded. The charts/ directory is empty. Helm can't resolve the dependency and the install fails with "no cached repository" or "chart not found." Your job: identify the missing dependency, run helm dependency update, and deploy successfully.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 6 (minikube) — Safe environment for dependency experiments
1

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost Chart — Missing Dependency BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost is a Django job board. In production, it relies on a PostgreSQL database. Instead of managing PostgreSQL manifests manually, the anihpj chart declares it as a Helm dependency — referencing the Bitnami PostgreSQL chart (version 15.x). This way, PostgreSQL upgrades, security patches, and configuration are managed by the upstream chart. But the developer forgot to run helm dependency update before committing — the charts/ directory is empty, and the Chart.lock file is missing. The entire anihpj/jobpost stack can't deploy because PostgreSQL is a hard dependency.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for anihpj Helm chart with dependency (S11): 
s11-chart/
├── Chart.yaml                          ← Declares PostgreSQL dependency ← BUG HERE!
├── values.yaml                         ← anihpj configuration
├── templates/
│   ├── _helpers.tpl                    ← Named templates
│   ├── NOTES.txt                       ← Post-install instructions
│   ├── namespace.yaml                  ← Namespace resource
│   ├── configmap.yaml                  ← Django settings ConfigMap
│   ├── django-api-deployment.yaml      ← Django API Deployment
│   ├── django-api-service.yaml         ← Django API Service
│   └── ingress.yaml                    ← Ingress for web + API
├── charts/                             ← ❌ EMPTY! Dependency not downloaded!
└── Chart.lock                          ← ❌ MISSING! No lock file!
BASH — Create chart with undeclared PostgreSQL dependency 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S11: Chart Dependency Failure — Missing PostgreSQL Subchart
# This is a STANDALONE lab — creates its own isolated chart directory.
# Run from any clean directory. No dependencies on other scenarios.

mkdir -p ~/helm-lab/s11-chart/charts
cd ~/helm-lab

apiVersion: v2

version: 1.0.0

# DEPENDENCIES — PostgreSQL subchart (Bitnami)

  - name: postgresql

{{- end -}}

{{- define "anihpj.selectorLabels" -}}

app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end -}}

cat << 'EOF' > ./s11-chart/templates/django-api-deployment.yaml

spec:

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. Run helm install anihpj ./s11-chart --dry-run → FAILS immediately!
✗2. Error: Error: found in Chart.yaml but missing in charts/ directory: postgresql
✗3. Check charts/ directory: ls ./s11-chart/charts/ → EMPTY!
✗4. Check for Chart.lock: ls ./s11-chart/Chart.lock → FILE NOT FOUND!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check Chart.yaml dependencies: grep -A5 "dependencies:" ./s11-chart/Chart.yaml
→ Declares postgresql v15.5.0 from Bitnami repo
2Check if dependency was downloaded: ls -la ./s11-chart/charts/
→ Directory exists but is EMPTY — no postgresql-15.5.0.tgz!
3Check if Chart.lock exists: ls ./s11-chart/Chart.lock
→ Chart.lock is MISSING — dependency update was never run!
4Root cause: Chart.yaml declares a dependency but helm dependency update was never executed. Helm requires dependencies to be physically present in charts/ before any install/template/lint operation. Without Chart.lock and the .tgz file, Helm refuses to proceed.
5Fix: Run helm dependency update ./s11-chart to download the PostgreSQL chart and generate Chart.lock
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm install fails → "missing in charts/"
②
Check Chart.yaml → Dependency declared
③
Check charts/ directory → Empty!
④
Check Chart.lock → Missing!
⑤
helm dependency update → Downloads chart → Deploy succeeds!

Tenet: Helm dependencies are NOT automatically resolved. Declaring a dependency in Chart.yaml is only the FIRST step. You MUST run helm dependency update (or helm dep up) to download the actual .tgz package into charts/ and generate Chart.lock. This is like npm install for Node.js or pip install -r requirements.txt for Python — the dependency declaration is just a manifest, not the actual code. In CI/CD, always run helm dependency update BEFORE helm package or helm install. The Chart.lock file should be committed to Git to ensure reproducible builds.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm install anihpj ./s11-chart --dry-run Error: found in Chart.yaml, but missing in charts/ directory: postgresql
$ ls -la ./s11-chart/charts/ total 0 drwxr-xr-x 2 owner owner 40 Jun 13 10:00 . drwxr-xr-x 4 owner owner 120 Jun 13 10:00 ..
$ ls ./s11-chart/Chart.lock ls: cannot access './s11-chart/Chart.lock': No such file or directory
$ helm lint ./s11-chart ==> Linting ./s11-chart [ERROR] Chart.yaml: dependency "postgresql" is not present in charts/ directory Error: 1 chart(s) linted, 1 chart(s) failed
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm dependency update ./s11-chart Hang tight while we grab the latest from your chart repositories... ...Successfully got an update from the "bitnami" chart repository Update Complete. ⎈Happy Helming!⎈ Saving 1 charts Downloading postgresql from repo https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami Deleting outdated charts
$ ls ./s11-chart/charts/ postgresql-15.5.0.tgz ✅ Dependency downloaded!
$ ls ./s11-chart/Chart.lock ./s11-chart/Chart.lock ✅ Lock file created!
$ helm install anihpj ./s11-chart --dry-run | head -3 --- # Source: anihpj/charts/postgresql/templates/secrets.yaml --- ✅ Chart renders successfully with dependency!
🔧
BASH — Download dependencies and rebuild chart 
# STEP 1: Add the Bitnami Helm repository (required for dependency resolution)
helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
helm repo update

# STEP 2: Download the dependency (this is THE fix)
cd ~/helm-lab
helm dependency update ./s11-chart

# STEP 3: Verify the dependency was downloaded
ls -la ./s11-chart/charts/
# Should show: postgresql-15.5.0.tgz

# STEP 4: Verify Chart.lock was generated
cat ./s11-chart/Chart.lock
# Should show: dependencies: [{name: postgresql, version: 15.5.0, repository: ...}]

# STEP 5: Build the chart dependencies (creates charts/ from lock)
helm dependency build ./s11-chart

# STEP 6: Verify the chart now passes linting
helm lint ./s11-chart

# STEP 7: Test render (dry-run)
helm install anihpj ./s11-chart --dry-run --debug 2>&1 | head -20

# GOLDEN RULES FOR HELM DEPENDENCIES:
# 1. Declare in Chart.yaml → helm dependency update → helm install
# 2. Always commit Chart.lock to Git (reproducible builds)
# 3. Run helm dependency update in CI/CD before helm package
# 4. Use helm dependency build if you have Chart.lock but no charts/

S12
🧪 SCENARIO S12 — Category 2: Chart Dependencies Upgrade Debug

helm upgrade Fails — Immutable StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplate Change

The Problem: anihpj/jobpost was deployed with a PostgreSQL StatefulSet using storageClassName: standard. The team wants to upgrade to storageClassName: fast-ssd. They update values.yaml and run helm upgrade anihpj ./s12-chart -n anihpj — but the upgrade FAILS. Kubernetes rejects the change because volumeClaimTemplates on a StatefulSet are immutable. Your job: understand WHY the upgrade failed, figure out the proper migration path (backup → delete → recreate → restore), and implement it.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 6 (minikube) — Has built-in StorageClass provisioner for reliable PVC binding
1

📋 Deploy anihpj PostgreSQL StatefulSet — THEN Attempt Upgrade with Changed StorageClass

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost uses a PostgreSQL StatefulSet for its database. The initial deployment used a hostPath-based StorageClass (local-path). The infrastructure team wants to upgrade to a new fast-ssd StorageClass backed by NVMe SSDs. The DevOps engineer updates values.yaml to change storageClassName: fast-ssd and runs helm upgrade. But Kubernetes blocks the upgrade — StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates are immutable after creation. The database is stuck on slow storage, and the upgrade process needs a full migration.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for anihpj StatefulSet chart (S12): 
s12-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml              ← storageClass: "local-path" initially
├── values-upgraded.yaml     ← storageClass: "fast-ssd" (THE UPGRADE ATTEMPT)
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl
    ├── storageclass.yaml     ← Creates local-path StorageClass (hostPath)
    ├── namespace.yaml
    ├── postgres-statefulset.yaml  ← volumeClaimTemplates — IMMUTABLE!
    └── postgres-service.yaml
BASH — Initial deployment + broken upgrade attempt 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S12: Immutable Field — StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates
# This is a STANDALONE lab — isolated chart directory.
# ============================================

# 1. CREATE FRESH PROJECT DIRECTORY
mkdir -p ~/helm-lab/s12-chart/templates
cd ~/helm-lab

# 0. CREATE LOCAL STORAGECLASS (hostPath — works on ANY cluster)
# This ensures the scenario works regardless of your cluster setup
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: local-path
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
EOF

# Create a hostPath PV so the PVC can bind
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/data/s12-postgres
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: s12-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: local-path
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data/s12-postgres
EOF

# 2. CREATE Chart.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: anihpj-db
description: PostgreSQL StatefulSet for anihpj/jobpost
type: application
version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "15"
EOF

# 3. CREATE INITIAL values.yaml (working deployment)
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/values.yaml
replicaCount: 1
postgres:
  image: postgres:15-alpine
  dbName: jobpost
  user: anihpj
  password: secret123
storage:
  className: "local-path"   # Initial StorageClass — hostPath-based
  size: 1Gi
service:
  port: 5432
EOF

# 4. CREATE _helpers.tpl
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "anihpj-db.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "anihpj-db.selectorLabels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end -}}
EOF

# 5. CREATE namespace.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/templates/namespace.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
EOF

# 6. CREATE postgres-statefulset.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/templates/postgres-statefulset.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres
spec:
  serviceName: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "anihpj-db.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "anihpj-db.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: {{ .Values.postgres.image }}
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              value: {{ .Values.postgres.dbName }}
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              value: {{ .Values.postgres.user }}
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              value: {{ .Values.postgres.password }}
            - name: PGDATA
              value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
          ports:
            - containerPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteOnce
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: {{ .Values.storage.size }}
        storageClassName: {{ .Values.storage.className }}
EOF

# 7. CREATE postgres-service.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/templates/postgres-service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-postgres
spec:
  selector:
    {{- include "anihpj-db.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}
  ports:
    - port: {{ .Values.service.port }}
      targetPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
EOF

# 8. INITIAL DEPLOYMENT (SUCCESSFUL)
echo "============================================"
echo "STEP 1: Initial deployment with standard StorageClass"
echo "============================================"
helm install anihpj-db ./s12-chart -n anihpj --create-namespace
echo ""
kubectl get pods -n anihpj
echo ""
kubectl get pvc -n anihpj
echo ""
echo "✅ PostgreSQL deployed with standard StorageClass"

# 9. NOW CREATE THE UPGRADED values.yaml (StorageClass changed!)
cat << 'EOF' > ./s12-chart/values-upgraded.yaml
storage:
  className: "fast-ssd"   # ❌ ATTEMPTED UPGRADE — This field is IMMUTABLE!
EOF

echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo "STEP 2: Attempting upgrade with fast-ssd StorageClass"
echo "THIS WILL FAIL because volumeClaimTemplates are immutable!"
echo "============================================"
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm upgrade anihpj-db ./s12-chart -n anihpj -f values-upgraded.yaml → FAILS!
✗2. Error: StatefulSet.apps "anihpj-db-postgres" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden
✗3. The PVC still shows STORAGECLASS: local-path — unchanged!
✗4. Database is still running on slow storage — upgrade path is BLOCKED!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Read the error carefully: helm upgrade ... 2>&1 | grep "Forbidden"
→ "updates to statefulset spec for fields other than ... are forbidden"
2Check Kubernetes documentation: kubectl explain statefulset.spec.volumeClaimTemplates
→ Once a StatefulSet is created, volumeClaimTemplates CANNOT be modified
3Check what fields ARE mutable: replicas, template (pod spec), updateStrategy, minReadySeconds
→ storageClassName is inside volumeClaimTemplates — which is NOT in the allowed list!
4Root cause: StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates are immutable by Kubernetes design. Once created, the PVC template CANNOT be changed — this prevents accidental data loss from changing underlying storage configurations. The only way to change StorageClass is: backup data → delete StatefulSet (--cascade=orphan to keep PVCs) → manually create new PVCs with new StorageClass → restore data → recreate StatefulSet pointing to new PVCs
5Migration path: This is NOT a Helm bug — it's a Kubernetes design constraint. The fix requires a multi-step data migration
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm upgrade fails → "updates forbidden"
②
Check what changed → volumeClaimTemplates
③
kubectl explain → IMMUTABLE field!
④
This is by design — protects data integrity
⑤
Migration: backup → cascade-orphan → new PVC → restore → redeploy

Tenet: StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates are immutable for a critical reason — changing the storage configuration of a running database could corrupt data. Kubernetes protects you from yourself. The correct migration path is: (1) Backup your data, (2) Delete the StatefulSet with --cascade=orphan (keeps PVCs and Pods), (3) Backup PVC data, (4) Create new PVCs with the new StorageClass, (5) Restore data to new PVCs, (6) Recreate StatefulSet referencing the new PVCs. This is the same pattern used in production database migrations. Helm can't automate this — it's an operational procedure.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm upgrade anihpj-db ./s12-chart -n anihpj -f values-upgraded.yaml Error: UPGRADE FAILED: cannot patch "anihpj-db-postgres" with kind StatefulSet: StatefulSet.apps "anihpj-db-postgres" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden
$ kubectl get pvc -n anihpj NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY STORAGECLASS data-anihpj-db-postgres-0 Bound pvc-abc123 1Gi standard ← UNCHANGED!
📟 Command Outputs — Migration Steps (AFTER fix)
$ kubectl delete sts anihpj-db-postgres -n anihpj --cascade=orphan statefulset.apps "anihpj-db-postgres" deleted ← PVCs preserved!
$ kubectl get pvc -n anihpj NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY STORAGECLASS data-anihpj-db-postgres-0 Bound pvc-abc123 1Gi standard ← Still here!
$ helm upgrade anihpj-db ./s12-chart -n anihpj -f values-upgraded.yaml --dry-run | grep storageClassName storageClassName: "fast-ssd" ✅ Chart now renders with new StorageClass!
🔧
BASH — Multi-step migration to change StorageClass 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STORAGE MIGRATION: standard → fast-ssd StorageClass
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# STEP 1: Backup PostgreSQL data
kubectl exec -n anihpj anihpj-db-postgres-0 -- pg_dump -U anihpj jobpost > ~/helm-lab/jobpost-backup.sql
echo "✅ Backup saved to ~/helm-lab/jobpost-backup.sql"

# STEP 2: Delete StatefulSet but KEEP PVCs and Pods (--cascade=orphan)
kubectl delete statefulset anihpj-db-postgres -n anihpj --cascade=orphan
echo "✅ StatefulSet deleted, PVCs and Pods preserved"

# STEP 3: Delete the pod (PVCs remain)
kubectl delete pod anihpj-db-postgres-0 -n anihpj --grace-period=0 --force
echo "✅ Pod deleted"

# STEP 4: Delete old PVCs
kubectl delete pvc data-anihpj-db-postgres-0 -n anihpj
echo "✅ Old PVC deleted"

# STEP 5: Create new PVC with fast-ssd StorageClass manually
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-anihpj-db-postgres-0
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
EOF
echo "✅ New PVC created with fast-ssd StorageClass"

# STEP 6: Re-deploy StatefulSet with updated chart
helm upgrade anihpj-db ./s12-chart -n anihpj -f values-upgraded.yaml --wait
echo "✅ StatefulSet recreated with new StorageClass"

# STEP 7: Verify new PVC uses fast-ssd
kubectl get pvc -n anihpj

# STEP 8: Restore data
kubectl exec -n anihpj anihpj-db-postgres-0 -- psql -U anihpj jobpost < ~/helm-lab/jobpost-backup.sql
echo "✅ Database restored on fast-ssd storage!"
🧹
BASH — copy & paste to clean up 
helm uninstall anihpj-db -n anihpj 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete pvc data-anihpj-db-postgres-0 -n anihpj 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete pv s12-pv 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete sc local-path 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete namespace anihpj 2>/dev/null
rm -rf ~/helm-lab/s12-chart
rm -f ~/helm-lab/jobpost-backup.sql
sudo rm -rf /mnt/data/s12-postgres
ls ~/helm-lab/s12-chart 2>/dev/null

🧪 SCENARIO S13 — Category 3: Release Lifecycle Hook Debug

helm install Hangs Forever — Pre-install Hook Fails (RBAC Missing)

The Problem: anihpj/jobpost chart includes a pre-install hook — a Kubernetes Job that runs database migrations before the Django API deployment starts. The hook Job is defined with "helm.sh/hook": pre-install annotation. But when you run helm install, it HANGS at "Running pre-install hooks" — the Job pod is stuck in Pending because its ServiceAccount doesn't have permissions to run the migration command. The ServiceAccount exists but has NO RoleBinding. Your job: identify the RBAC gap, grant the ServiceAccount the necessary permissions, and complete the deployment.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — RBAC-safe environment for hook debugging
1

📋 Deploy anihpj/jobpost Chart with Pre-install Migration Hook — RBAC BUG

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost uses Django database migrations to manage schema changes. The DevOps team created a Helm pre-install hook: a Kubernetes Job that runs python manage.py migrate BEFORE the Django API pods start. This ensures the database schema is always up-to-date before the application tries to connect. The hook Job uses a dedicated ServiceAccount anihpj-migration-sa to interact with the Kubernetes API (to wait for PostgreSQL readiness). But the ServiceAccount has no RoleBinding — it can't list pods or check services. The hook pod is stuck in Pending, and the Helm install hangs indefinitely. The entire job board deployment is blocked by a missing RBAC rule.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for anihpj Helm chart with migration hook (S13): 
s13-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl
    ├── namespace.yaml
    ├── serviceaccount.yaml          ← ServiceAccount for migration hook
    ├── configmap.yaml                ← Database migration script
    ├── hook-pre-install-db-migrate.yaml  ← Pre-install Job Hook ← BUG HERE!
    ├── django-api-deployment.yaml    ← Django API (waits for hook)
    └── django-api-service.yaml
BASH — Create chart with broken pre-install hook (missing RBAC) 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S13: Pre-install Hook Failure — Missing RBAC
# This is a STANDALONE lab — isolated chart directory.
# ============================================

# 1. CREATE FRESH PROJECT DIRECTORY
mkdir -p ~/helm-lab/s13-chart/templates
cd ~/helm-lab

# 2. CREATE Chart.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: anihpj-migrate
description: anihpj/jobpost with pre-install DB migration hook
type: application
version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "2.5"
EOF

# 3. CREATE values.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/values.yaml
hookTimeout: 300
dbHost: "postgres"
dbPort: 5432
image:
  repository: anihpj-api
  tag: latest
service:
  port: 8000
EOF

# 4. CREATE _helpers.tpl
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "anihpj-migrate.labels" -}}
app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
{{- end -}}
EOF

# 5. CREATE namespace.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/namespace.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
EOF

# 6. CREATE serviceaccount.yaml — Migration hook SA (NO RoleBinding!)
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/serviceaccount.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: anihpj-migration-sa
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj-migrate.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
# ❌ BUG! No Role or RoleBinding created for this ServiceAccount!
# The hook Job references this SA, but it has zero permissions!
EOF

# 7. CREATE configmap.yaml — Migration script
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/configmap.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-migration-script
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-5"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
data:
  migrate.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    echo "============================================"
    echo "PRE-INSTALL HOOK: Database Migration"
    echo "============================================"
    echo "Waiting for PostgreSQL at {{ .Values.dbHost }}:{{ .Values.dbPort }}..."
    sleep 10
    echo "Checking Kubernetes API for PostgreSQL pod readiness..."
    kubectl get pods -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} -l app=postgres
    echo ""
    echo "Running Django database migrations..."
    echo "python manage.py migrate --noinput"
    echo ""
    echo "✅ Database migration complete!"
    echo "============================================"
EOF

# 8. CREATE hook-pre-install-db-migrate.yaml — Pre-install Job Hook
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/hook-pre-install-db-migrate.yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-db-migrate
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "0"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  activeDeadlineSeconds: {{ .Values.hookTimeout }}
  template:
    metadata:
      name: {{ .Release.Name }}-db-migrate
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: anihpj-migration-sa  # ❌ SA with NO permissions!
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: db-migrate
          image: bitnami/kubectl:latest  # Has kubectl built-in for API calls
          command: ["/bin/sh", "/scripts/migrate.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: migration-script
              mountPath: /scripts
      volumes:
        - name: migration-script
          configMap:
            name: {{ .Release.Name }}-migration-script
            defaultMode: 0755
EOF

# 9. CREATE django-api-deployment.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/django-api-deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
  labels:
    {{- include "anihpj-migrate.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": post-install
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "5"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "anihpj-migrate.labels" . | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "anihpj-migrate.labels" . | nindent 8 }}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
          ports:
            - containerPort: {{ .Values.service.port }}
EOF

# 10. CREATE django-api-service.yaml
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/django-api-service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api
spec:
  selector:
    {{- include "anihpj-migrate.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  ports:
    - port: {{ .Values.service.port }}
EOF

echo "============================================"
echo "CHART CREATED — Attempting helm install..."
echo "THIS WILL HANG because the hook Job ServiceAccount"
echo "has NO RBAC permissions to run kubectl commands!"
echo "============================================"
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm install anihpj-migrate ./s13-chart -n anihpj --create-namespace --timeout 2m → HANGS and eventually TIMES OUT!
✗2. Output: Running pre-install hooks... (stuck here for 2 minutes)
✗3. Check hook Job: kubectl get jobs -n anihpj → COMPLETIONS: 0/1
✗4. Check hook pod: kubectl logs job/anihpj-migrate-db-migrate -n anihpj → shows "Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden"
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check hook Job status: kubectl describe job anihpj-migrate-db-migrate -n anihpj
→ Pod status: "Failed" — BackoffLimit reached
2Check hook pod logs: kubectl logs -l job-name=anihpj-migrate-db-migrate -n anihpj
→ "Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User ... cannot list resource 'pods'"
3Check ServiceAccount permissions: kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:anihpj:anihpj-migration-sa -n anihpj
→ "no" — The ServiceAccount has ZERO permissions!
4Check for RoleBindings: kubectl get rolebinding -n anihpj
→ No RoleBindings exist for anihpj-migration-sa
5Root cause: The pre-install hook Job uses a ServiceAccount that has NO RBAC permissions. The ServiceAccount exists but has no Role or RoleBinding granting it the ability to list pods or check services. The hook script calls kubectl get pods which is denied by the API server.
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm install hangs → Pre-install hook stuck
②
Check hook Job → BackoffLimit reached
③
Check pod logs → "Forbidden: pods is forbidden"
④
Check RBAC → SA has no RoleBinding!
⑤
Create Role + RoleBinding → Hook succeeds → Deploy continues!

Tenet: Helm hooks run as Kubernetes Jobs with a ServiceAccount. That ServiceAccount needs explicit RBAC permissions to interact with the Kubernetes API. A ServiceAccount without a RoleBinding is like a user without a login — it exists but can't do anything. When creating hook Jobs that need to query the cluster (check pod readiness, list services, verify ConfigMaps), you MUST create a Role (granting get/list permissions) and a RoleBinding (linking the Role to the ServiceAccount). Without this, every kubectl command in the hook fails with "Forbidden."

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm install anihpj-migrate ./s13-chart -n anihpj --create-namespace --timeout 2m NAME: anihpj-migrate LAST DEPLOYED: Fri Jun 13 10:00:00 2026 NAMESPACE: anihpj STATUS: deployed REVISION: 1 TEST SUITE: None NOTES: Error: timed out waiting for the condition
$ kubectl get jobs -n anihpj NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE anihpj-migrate-db-migrate 0/1 2m 2m
$ kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:anihpj:anihpj-migration-sa -n anihpj no ← ServiceAccount has ZERO permissions!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:anihpj:anihpj-migration-sa -n anihpj yes ✅ ServiceAccount now authorized!
$ kubectl get jobs -n anihpj NAME COMPLETIONS DURATION AGE anihpj-migrate-db-migrate 1/1 15s 30s ✅ Hook completed!
🔧
BASH — Grant RBAC permissions to hook ServiceAccount 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RBAC FIX: Grant ServiceAccount permissions to query pods
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# STEP 1: Clean up the failed release first
helm uninstall anihpj-migrate -n anihpj 2>/dev/null

# STEP 2: Create a Role granting pod+service get/list permissions
kubectl create role migration-runner \
  --verb=get,list \
  --resource=pods,services,configmaps \
  -n anihpj

# STEP 3: Bind the Role to the ServiceAccount
kubectl create rolebinding migration-runner-binding \
  --role=migration-runner \
  --serviceaccount=anihpj:anihpj-migration-sa \
  -n anihpj

# STEP 4: Verify permissions
kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:anihpj:anihpj-migration-sa -n anihpj

# STEP 5: Retry the Helm install
helm install anihpj-migrate ./s13-chart -n anihpj --create-namespace --timeout 3m

# STEP 6: Verify hook completed
kubectl get jobs -n anihpj
kubectl logs job/anihpj-migrate-db-migrate -n anihpj

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# LONG-TERM FIX: Add RBAC to the chart templates
# Create templates/rbac.yaml in your chart:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cat << 'EOF' > ./s13-chart/templates/rbac.yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-hook-role
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-10"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods", "services", "configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-hook-rolebinding
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-10"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: anihpj-migration-sa
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-hook-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF

echo "✅ RBAC templates added to chart for future deployments!"
🧹
BASH — copy & paste to clean up 
helm uninstall anihpj-migrate -n anihpj 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete rolebinding migration-runner-binding -n anihpj 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete role migration-runner -n anihpj 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete namespace anihpj 2>/dev/null
rm -rf ~/helm-lab/s13-chart
ls ~/helm-lab/s13-chart 2>/dev/null

→ null — the "database" key doesn't exist at all!
3Understand Go template nil handling: In Go templates, accessing a field on a nil map/struct causes a PANIC, not an empty string
→ Unlike Python (AttributeError) or JavaScript (undefined), Go PANICS — the whole template crashes!
4Root cause: values.yaml is missing the entire "database:" section. The templates reference .Values.database.password, .Values.database.host, etc., but .Values.database is nil. Go's template engine panics when dereferencing a nil pointer — there's no graceful fallback.
5Fix: Add the database: section to values.yaml with all required fields, and use required function for mandatory values
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm template panics → "nil pointer evaluating"
②
Read error location → secret.yaml line 8
③
Check values.yaml → database section MISSING!
④
Go templates PANIC on nil — no graceful fallback
⑤
Add database section + required validation → Chart renders!

Tenet: "nil pointer evaluating" is the #2 most common Helm error after template syntax errors. It means your template is trying to access a field on something that doesn't exist. In Go templates, {{ .Values.database.password }} will PANIC if database is not defined in values.yaml. The fix is twofold: (1) Add the missing section to values.yaml, and (2) Use the required function for mandatory values: {{ required "database.password is required" .Values.database.password }}. This gives a clear error message instead of a cryptic nil pointer panic. For optional values, use {{ .Values.database.password | default "defaultpass" }} to provide fallbacks.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm template test ./s14-chart Error: template: anihpj-secure/templates/secret.yaml:8:56: executing "anihpj-secure/templates/secret.yaml" at <.Values.database.password>: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.password
$ yq eval '.database' ./s14-chart/values.yaml null ← database section does not exist!
$ helm lint ./s14-chart ==> Linting ./s14-chart [ERROR] templates/: template: anihpj-secure/templates/secret.yaml:8:56: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.password Error: 1 chart(s) linted, 1 chart(s) failed
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s14-chart | head -10 --- # Source: anihpj-secure/templates/secret.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata: name: test-db-secret type: Opaque stringData: database-url: "postgresql://anihpj:secret123@anihpj-db:5432/jobpost" ✅
$ helm lint ./s14-chart ==> Linting ./s14-chart 1 chart(s) linted, 0 chart(s) failed ✅
🔧
BASH — Add database values and use required for validation 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FIX: Add missing database section to values.yaml
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

cat << 'EOF' >> ./s14-chart/values.yaml

# Database configuration (REQUIRED)
database:
  host: "anihpj-db"
  port: 5432
  name: "jobpost"
  user: "anihpj"
  password: "secret123"
EOF

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# BEST PRACTICE: Add required validation in templates
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Update secret.yaml to use "required" for mandatory values:
cat << 'EOF' > ./s14-chart/templates/secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-db-secret
type: Opaque
stringData:
  database-url: "postgresql://{{ required "database.user is required" .Values.database.user }}:{{ required "database.password is required" .Values.database.password }}@{{ required "database.host is required" .Values.database.host }}:{{ .Values.database.port | default 5432 }}/{{ required "database.name is required" .Values.database.name }}"
EOF

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# VERIFY: Test render with corrected chart
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Should render successfully now:
helm template test ./s14-chart
echo "---"
helm lint ./s14-chart

# Test that "required" validation works (temporarily remove password):
yq eval 'del(.database.password)' ./s14-chart/values.yaml > /tmp/test-values.yaml
helm template test ./s14-chart -f /tmp/test-values.yaml 2>&1 || true
# Should print: "database.password is required" — clear error!

echo ""
echo "✅ Chart now renders with proper validation!"

Tenet: Named template names in Helm are fully case-sensitive — they're Go template names, not Kubernetes resource names. "anihpj.Labels", "anihpj.labels", and "ANihPJ.LABELS" are three completely different templates. The convention is ALL lowercase with dots as separators: "anihpj.labels", "anihpj.selectorLabels", "anihpj.fullname". Follow this convention religiously. When you get "template not defined," the first thing to check is: (1) Does the define exist? (2) Is the name spelled exactly the same (case, punctuation, whitespace)? (3) Is the _helpers.tpl file actually being picked up (check it's in templates/)?

.Files.Get Returns Empty — Missing Config File Causes Identical Checksums

The Problem: The anihpj/jobpost chart uses {{ .Files.Get "config/app.conf" | sha256sum }} to generate unique ConfigMap checksums for rolling updates. But config/app.conf doesn't exist in the chart! .Files.Get silently returns an empty string for missing files, so EVERY ConfigMap gets the SAME checksum hash. When you change values, the Deployment doesn't restart because the checksum hasn't changed. Your job: find why ConfigMap checksums are identical, verify the file path, and fix the rolling update mechanism.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — Template rendering, no cluster deployment needed
1

📋 Create Chart with Broken .Files.Get Reference

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost stores Django application settings in a ConfigMap. To trigger automatic pod restarts when settings change, the chart adds a checksum annotation: checksum/config: {{ .Files.Get "config/app.conf" | sha256sum }}. But the developer typed the file path wrong — config/app.conf doesn't exist; the actual file is config/app.ini. .Files.Get doesn't error on missing files — it returns empty string. So EVERY deployment annotation gets sha256sum("") — the same hash! Pods never restart on config changes, and production runs with stale settings.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for anihpj Helm chart (S16): 
s16-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml
├── config/
│   └── app.ini               ← Actual file (exists)
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl
    ├── configmap.yaml          ← References config/app.conf ← FILE DOESN'T EXIST!
    └── deployment.yaml         ← Uses checksum annotation — always SAME!

EOF

  repository: nginx

  port: 80

  debug: "false"
  logLevel: "info"

# CREATE THE ACTUAL config file (correct path: config/app.ini)

cat << 'EOF' > ./s16-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "anihpj-files.labels" -}}

{{- end -}}

# configmap.yaml — references NON-EXISTENT file!
cat << 'EOF' > ./s16-chart/templates/configmap.yaml

  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-django-config

cat << 'EOF' > ./s16-chart/templates/deployment.yaml

  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-api

echo "============================================"
echo "CHART CREATED — Now rendering to check checksum..."
echo "config/app.conf does NOT exist — .Files.Get"
echo "will silently return empty string!"
echo "============================================"

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s16-chart | grep "checksum/config" → Shows SAME hash for ConfigMap AND Deployment!
✗2. Run with different values: helm template test ./s16-chart --set appConfig.debug=true → Checksum STILL the same!
✗3. The checksum is e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 — that's sha256 of EMPTY string!
✗4. Pods NEVER restart on config changes — production runs with stale Django settings!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check the checksum value: helm template test ./s16-chart | grep "checksum"
→ e3b0c442... — this is sha256("") — the hash of an EMPTY string!
2Check what file .Files.Get references: grep "Files.Get" ./s16-chart/templates/configmap.yaml
→ References "config/app.conf" — does this file exist?
3List files in config/ directory: ls -la ./s16-chart/config/
→ Only "app.ini" exists — "app.conf" does NOT exist!
4Root cause: .Files.Get("config/app.conf") references a file that doesn't exist in the chart. .Files.Get silently returns an empty string for missing files — Helm does NOT error or warn. The sha256sum of the empty string is always the same, so all ConfigMaps and Deployments get identical checksum annotations. Rolling updates based on config changes are completely broken.
5Fix: Change the path from "config/app.conf" to "config/app.ini" (the actual file), or add the missing config/app.conf file to the chart
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Checksums all identical → Something is wrong
②
Hash matches sha256("") → .Files.Get returns empty
③
Check file path → config/app.conf doesn't exist!
④
Fix path to app.ini → Real checksums generated
⑤
Rolling updates work — pods restart on config changes!

Tenet: .Files.Get is a SILENT failure function — it returns an empty string if the file doesn't exist, with NO error or warning. This is by design (non-essential files shouldn't break the chart), but it means you MUST verify file existence. Always: (1) Double-check file paths in .Files.Get calls, (2) Use {{ if .Files.Get "path" }}{{ .Files.Get "path" | sha256sum }}{{ end }} to guard against missing files, (3) Know that sha256("") = e3b0c442... — if you see this hash, .Files.Get returned empty.

$ helm template test ./s16-chart | grep "checksum" checksum/config: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 checksum/config: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 ← Both ConfigMap and Deployment have the SAME hash! sha256("")!
$ echo -n "" | sha256sum e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 - ← PROOF: This is sha256 of empty!
$ ls -la ./s16-chart/config/ -rw-r--r-- 1 owner owner 65 Jun 13 10:00 app.ini ← Only app.ini exists! ← config/app.conf DOES NOT EXIST!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s16-chart | grep "checksum" checksum/config: a1b2c3d4e5f6... ← ConfigMap checksum (app.ini hash) checksum/config: a1b2c3d4e5f6... ← Deployment checksum matches ✅

# Verify the fix
helm template test ./s16-chart | grep "checksum/config"
echo ""
echo "✅ Checksums now derived from actual file content!"

lookup Function Breaks --dry-run — Output Differs From Real Install

The Problem: The anihpj chart uses {{ lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "db-creds" }} to fetch an existing database Secret and include its password in the deployment. The chart renders fine with --dry-run, but the output is DIFFERENT from the actual install — during dry-run, lookup returns nil (no real API server), so the template produces incomplete YAML. When you actually install, the template suddenly works because the Secret exists. This breaks CI/CD validation — you can't trust dry-run output. Your job: understand why lookup is dangerous, replace it with explicit values, and make dry-run reliable.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — Template rendering comparison
1

📋 Create Chart That Uses lookup — Broken for --dry-run

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost needs a database password that already exists as a Kubernetes Secret named db-creds. A developer uses {{ lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "db-creds" }} to fetch it dynamically during template rendering. During --dry-run in CI/CD, the lookup returns nil (no live cluster to query), so the template renders empty values. During actual helm install, the lookup works and returns real data. CI/CD validation passes a "broken" template because dry-run and real-install produce DIFFERENT output — a dangerous false positive!
📁 FILE STRUCTURE (S17): 
s17-chart/
├── Chart.yaml
├── values.yaml
└── templates/
    ├── _helpers.tpl
    ├── configmap.yaml          ← Uses lookup to fetch Secret — BROKEN for --dry-run!
    └── deployment.yaml

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Compare dry-run output: helm template test ./s17-chart | grep DATABASE_PASSWORD
→ DATABASE_PASSWORD: "" — empty because lookup returns nil during dry-run!
2Check what lookup does: lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "db-creds"
→ This makes a LIVE API call to the Kubernetes API server — during dry-run, there IS no API server!
3Understand lookup behavior: During helm template or --dry-run, lookup returns nil. During actual install, it queries the live cluster
→ This means dry-run output is NEVER identical to real install output!
4Root cause: The lookup function breaks Helm's declarative model. Helm templates should produce the SAME output regardless of whether it's dry-run or real install. lookup makes the template IMPERATIVE — its output depends on cluster state. This breaks CI/CD validation, GitOps diffing, and reproducibility.
5Fix: Replace lookup with explicit values — pass the database password via values.yaml or --set instead of querying the live cluster
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Dry-run shows empty password → Real install shows password
②
Output differs → lookup is the culprit
③
lookup queries live API → nil during dry-run
④
Replace with explicit values → Consistent output
⑤
Dry-run == Real install → CI/CD validation reliable!

Tenet: lookup is Helm's escape hatch for querying the live Kubernetes API during template rendering. It breaks the declarative model — the same chart produces different output depending on cluster state. AVOID lookup in production templates. Instead, pass ALL external data through values.yaml, --set, or External Secrets Operator. lookup is only acceptable in post-install hooks or NOTES.txt (where dry-run consistency doesn't matter). If you MUST use lookup, always wrap it in {{ if $result := lookup ... }}{{ else }}{{ end }} with explicit fallbacks.

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check which API is selected: helm template test ./s18-chart | grep "apiVersion"
→ apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1 — WRONG! Should be networking.k8s.io/v1!
2Check the semverCompare condition: grep "semverCompare" ./s18-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
→ semverCompare ">=1.19-0" .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion
3Check what .GitVersion contains: kubectl version --short shows "v1.30.0" — the 'v' prefix!
→ semverCompare can't parse "v1.30.0" — it needs "1.30.0" without the 'v'!
4Root cause: .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion returns the git tag format like "v1.32.13", NOT SemVer format. semverCompare requires SemVer without the 'v' prefix. The correct field is .Capabilities.KubeVersion.Version which returns "1.32.13" — proper SemVer. Because the comparison always fails, the {{ else }} branch always executes, selecting the legacy API.
5Fix: Change .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion to .Capabilities.KubeVersion.Version
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Legacy API selected → Version check must be failing
②
Check semverCompare → Uses .GitVersion
③
.GitVersion has 'v' prefix → semverCompare rejects it
④
Switch to .Version → Proper SemVer comparison
⑤
Correct API selected → No deprecation warnings!

Tenet: .Capabilities.KubeVersion has FOUR fields: .Version (SemVer: "1.32.13"), .GitVersion (git tag: "v1.32.13"), .Major ("1"), .Minor ("32"). For semverCompare, ALWAYS use .Version or .Major/.Minor. NEVER use .GitVersion — the 'v' prefix breaks semantic version parsing. This is the #1 cause of "my Kubernetes version detection doesn't work" in Helm charts. The fields look similar but behave differently in template functions.

📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s18-chart | grep "apiVersion" apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 ✅ Correct! Modern Ingress API!
🔧

echo ""
echo "✅ Now using networking.k8s.io/v1!"

📋 Create Chart with Wrong Scope in include Inside range

But inside range, the dot (.) is the current database item — it doesn't have .Release, .Chart, or .Values! The db-service template panics trying to access {{ .Release.Name }}. ⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s19-chart 2>&1 | head -5 → PANICS! "nil pointer evaluating interface {}.Release"
✗2. The error comes from db-service trying to access .Release.Name — but "." is a database item!
✗3. The same would happen for .Chart.Name, .Values.* — all root-level fields are inaccessible inside range!
✗4. Multi-database support is completely BROKEN — chart can't even render!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Read the error: helm template test ./s19-chart 2>&1
→ "nil pointer evaluating interface {}.Release" — db-service can't find .Release!
2Check what "." is inside range: In {{ range .Values.databases }}, "." is reassigned to the current item — a database object with {name, port, type}
→ db-service receives a database item as context, NOT the root!
3Check include's second argument: {{ include "db-service" . }} — the dot after the template name IS the scope passed
→ Whatever "." is at that point becomes the template's scope!
4Root cause: Inside {{ range }}, the dot "." is reassigned to the loop variable (current item). When include passes "." as scope, the called template receives the item, NOT the root. The solution: save the root scope BEFORE the range loop with {{ $ := . }} (or {{ $root := . }}), then pass $ to include: {{ include "db-service" (merge . $) }} or restructure the template to accept both scopes.
5Fix: Save root with {{- $root := . -}} before range, then use {{ include "db-service" (merge . $root) }} or pass $root directly
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
helm template panics → "nil pointer .Release"
②
Error in db-service → Called from inside range
③
range reassigns "." → db-service gets item, not root
④
Save root with $ → Pass $ to include
⑤
All database services render correctly!

Tenet: In Go templates, range, with, and if all reassign the dot "." to their pipeline value. Inside a block, "." is NOT the root anymore. To access the root inside these blocks, save it with {{ $ := . }} (or {{ $root := . }}) BEFORE the block. When calling include, the second argument IS the scope — choose wisely: {{ include "my-template" . }} passes current scope, {{ include "my-template" $ }} passes saved root. For templates that need BOTH item data and root data, use {{ include "my-template" (merge (dict "item" .) $) }} or restructure the template to accept explicit parameters.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm template test ./s19-chart 2>&1 Error: template: anihpj-scope/templates/_helpers.tpl:5:18: executing "anihpj-scope/templates/_helpers.tpl" at <.Release.Name>: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.Release
$ grep -A3 "range .Values.databases" ./s19-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl {{- range .Values.databases }} --- {{ include "db-service" . }} ← "." is a database item {name, port, type}!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ helm template test ./s19-chart 2>&1 | grep -c "kind: Service" 3 ← 3 database services rendered successfully! ✅
🔧
BASH — Fix scope by saving root before range
# FIX: Save root scope with $ before range, pass $ to include
cat << 'EOF' > ./s19-chart/templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "db-service" }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .root.Release.Name }}-{{ .item.name }}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .root.Chart.Name }}
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .root.Release.Name }}
    db-type: {{ .item.type }}
spec:
  selector:
    app: {{ .root.Release.Name }}-{{ .item.name }}
  ports:
    - port: {{ .item.port }}
      targetPort: {{ .item.port }}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "anihpj-scope.allDbServices" }}
{{- $root := . }}
{{- range .Values.databases }}
---
{{ include "db-service" (dict "item" . "root" $root) }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ./s19-chart/templates/db-services.yaml
{{ include "anihpj-scope.allDbServices" . }}
EOF

# Verify the fix
helm template test ./s19-chart | grep "kind: Service"
echo ""
echo "✅ All 3 database services rendered with correct scoping!"

⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. helm template test ./s20-chart → RENDERS SUCCESSFULLY! No validation error at all!
✗2. helm template test ./s20-chart --set replicaCount=5 → Still renders! database values are the DEFAULTS from values.yaml!
✗3. The rendered ConfigMap shows DATABASE_HOST: "localhost" — the DEFAULT from values.yaml, NOT what the user intended!
✗4. Django connects to "localhost" instead of the actual PostgreSQL service — deployment succeeds but application is MISCONFIGURED!
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check if schema validation runs: helm lint ./s20-chart
→ Lint passes — no errors! Schema validation reports no issues!
2Understand Helm's value merging order: (1) values.yaml defaults → (2) parent chart values → (3) user --set/--values → (4) schema validation
→ Schema validates the MERGED result, which ALREADY includes values.yaml defaults!
3Check if required fields exist after merge: values.yaml provides "replicaCount: 1" and "database: {...}" → all required fields are present after merge
→ Schema validation sees ALL required fields because values.yaml fills them in!
4Root cause: Helm's JSON schema validation runs on the FINAL merged values (values.yaml defaults + user overrides). If values.yaml provides defaults for required fields, the schema will NEVER detect missing user input — the defaults always satisfy the "required" constraint. The schema only catches TYPE errors (e.g., passing a string where an integer is expected), not MISSING values that have defaults.
5Fix: Remove defaults for truly mandatory fields from values.yaml and use {{ required "message" .Values.database.host }} in templates, OR keep defaults but add additional validation (e.g., require host != "localhost" for production)
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Schema defines required fields → Deploy without them
②
Deploy succeeds → Schema didn't catch missing values!
③
values.yaml provides defaults → Merge fills required fields
④
Schema validates merged result → All fields present → PASSES!
⑤
Use required() function → Fails fast with clear message!

Tenet: Helm's JSON schema validation validates the MERGED values (values.yaml + user overrides), not just user input. If values.yaml provides defaults for required fields, the schema will never reject missing user input. The schema is useful for TYPE validation (string vs integer, enum values, patterns) but NOT for detecting missing mandatory configuration. For truly required values, use {{ required "database.host is required for production" .Values.database.host }} in templates — this fails fast with a clear error message. Combine both: schema for type safety, required for mandatory values.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ helm template test ./s20-chart 2>&1 | grep DATABASE DATABASE_HOST: "localhost" ← DEFAULT from values.yaml — user may not realize this! DATABASE_PORT: "5432" DATABASE_NAME: "jobpost" DATABASE_USER: "anihpj" DATABASE_PASSWORD: "defaultpass" ← DEFAULT password — SECURITY RISK!
$ helm lint ./s20-chart ==> Linting ./s20-chart 1 chart(s) linted, 0 chart(s) failed ← Schema validation PASSES!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix (required function)
$ helm template test ./s20-chart --set database.host="" Error: execution error at (anihpj-schema/templates/configmap.yaml:...): database.host must be set to a non-empty value for production use ✅
🔧
BASH — Add required() calls for truly mandatory values
# FIX: Use required() function for mandatory production values
cat << 'EOF' > ./s20-chart/templates/configmap.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-django-config
data:
  DATABASE_HOST: {{ required "database.host must be set for production" .Values.database.host | quote }}
  DATABASE_PORT: {{ .Values.database.port | default 5432 | quote }}
  DATABASE_NAME: {{ required "database.name is required" .Values.database.name | quote }}
  DATABASE_USER: {{ required "database.user is required" .Values.database.user | quote }}
  DATABASE_PASSWORD: {{ required "database.password is required — never use defaults in production!" .Values.database.password | quote }}
EOF

# Verify: deploy WITHOUT database values — should FAIL now
echo "=== Testing with missing database values ==="
helm template test ./s20-chart --set database.password="" 2>&1 || true
echo ""
echo "✅ required() function now catches missing values!"
🧹
BASH — copy & paste to clean up
rm -rf ~/helm-lab/s20-chart
ls ~/helm-lab/s20-chart 2>/dev/null

helm upgrade Wipes Custom Values — --reuse-values Forgotten

1

📋 Deploy with Custom Values — Then Upgrade WITHOUT --reuse-values
